text: Tests organized three tiers: Pure unit tests (test-health_response.R): response construction, serialization, validation. request objects, server. App-object introspection tests (test-add_healthcheck.R): add_healthcheck() shiny.appobj (class, metadata attribute, handler replacement, stacking). server, fabricated shiny request objects – request-shaped inputs ever exercised real running app. Wire tests (test-wire.R, test-wire-process.R): live app served via non-blocking shiny::startApp(), probed real HTTP requests. IMPORTANT (wire tests): synchronous httr2::req_perform() app served startApp() R session deadlock – curl blocks R thread, thread later event loop needs run app’s HTTP handler. Requests must performed promises (httr2::req_perform_promise()) event loop pumped via later::run_now() resolution. See tests/testthat/helper.R (fetch_url()). cross-process variant (test-wire-process.R) runs blocking client callr::r_bg() child process parent pumps event loop serve .

title: Getting Started
text: Deployment platforms decide whether application working probing HTTP endpoint: Kubernetes uses liveness readiness probes; status code >= 200 < 400 counts success, anything else failure. Google Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps, AWS load balancers behave way – HTTP status code contract. failing liveness probe restarts container; failing readiness probe stops routing traffic . Shiny native concept health endpoint, common workarounds (wrapping UI function, adjusting uiPattern, running plumber sidecar) easy get wrong – misconfigured uiPattern silently 404s every probe, health check behind authentication wrapper bounces probes sign-page. shinyhealth solves right layer: app object’s HTTP handler, requests can intercepted UI rendering, session creation, authentication.

title: Getting Started
text: Pipe Shiny app object add_healthcheck(): decorated app answers GET /health JSON response passes every request app unchanged. uiPattern adjustment needed, construction method matter – plain shiny::shinyApp(), golem, apps wrapped authentication packages like polished work, interception happens app object fully constructed. Probing endpoint returns:
code: app <- shiny::shinyApp(   ui = shiny::fluidPage("hello"),   server = function(input, output, session) {} ) |>   add_healthcheck()  has_healthcheck(app) #> [1] TRUE healthcheck_paths(app) #> [1] "/health" $ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/health+json Cache-Control: no-store  {"status":"pass","timestamp":"2026-09-06T23:00:17Z"}

title: Getting Started
text: health_response() builds response objects served health endpoints. defaults produce healthy response: Two fields deliberately independent: status_code (HTTP transport status) orchestrators interpret. 200 means healthy; 503 (Service Unavailable) standard choice unhealthy. status (body field) convention humans tooling. default vocabulary ("pass", convention "warn" / "fail") follows IETF health check response format draft, value accepted. response defaults follow relevant standards: application/health+json content type (safe JSON consumer per RFC 6839’s +json suffix rule), Cache-Control: -store probe responses never cached, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps. Additional named fields merge body, checks carries arbitrarily nested check results:
code: health_response() health_response(status = "fail", status_code = 503L) health_response(   version = "1.0.0",   checks = list(     database = list(status = "pass", latency_ms = 2.3),     upstream_api = list(status = "warn", output = "slow response times")   ) )

code: handler <- function(req) {   list(status = "degraded", status_code = 503L, reason = "cache warming") }  as_health_response(handler(req = NULL))

title: Getting Started
text: Registrations stack, separate endpoints different handlers just repeated calls: common pattern: keep liveness handler trivial (default – process can answer, alive) put dependency checks readiness endpoint, database blip stops traffic routing without triggering container restarts.
code: app <- shiny::shinyApp(   ui = shiny::fluidPage("hello"),   server = function(input, output, session) {} ) |>   add_healthcheck(path = "/livez") |>   add_healthcheck(path = "/readyz", handler = function(req) {     health_response(       checks = list(database = list(status = "pass"))     )   })  healthcheck_paths(app) #> [1] "/livez"  "/readyz"

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: health_response(), new_health_response(), as_health_response() return health_response object (classed shiny::httpResponse()). validate_health_response() invisibly returns input valid, otherwise throws check_error condition. is_health_response() returns logical scalar.

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: HTTP transport status (status_code) body status field deliberately independent: Orchestrators load balancers (Kubernetes, Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps, etc.) interpret HTTP status code: codes >= 200 < 400 indicate success, anything else indicates failure. body status string convention humans tooling. default value ("pass") follows IETF health check response format draft (draft-inadarei-api-health-check, also suggests "warn" "fail"), value accepted – use whatever vocabulary fits conventions. defaults compose healthy response (status = "pass", status_code = 200L). unhealthy response, 503L (Service Unavailable) standard choice, typically paired status = "fail". individual checks aggregate overall status intentionally decided – policy belongs handler builds response.

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: Default headers Cache-Control: -store (RFC 9111) probe responses never cached. legacy Pragma/Expires response headers deprecated RFC 9111 intentionally omitted. CORS headers sent default (probes server--server); supply via headers browser client another origin needs access. default content type application/health+json per IETF draft. +json structured syntax suffix (RFC 6839) guarantees JSON processor handles ; use content_type override (e.g. plain application/json). Timestamps use RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 format UTC (see ts_utc()).

title: Health Check Response — health_response
code: # healthy response with defaults health_response()  # unhealthy response (standard choice: 503 + "fail") health_response(status = "fail", status_code = 503L)  # custom vocabulary, extra fields, and nested checks health_response(   status = "HEALTHY",   version = "1.0.0",   checks = list(     database = list(status = "pass", latency_ms = 2.3),     api = list(status = "warn", output = "slow response times")   ) )
